templates.refund:
Refund & Return Policy for {shop}:

1. Timeframe:
Customers may request a return or exchange within 14 days of receiving their order.

2. Return Conditions:
- The product must be unused, in its original packaging with all tags and accessories attached.
- A proof of purchase or order confirmation must be provided.
- Perishable goods, personalized items, and personal care products are non-returnable.

3. Refunds:
Once returned items are received and inspected, refunds will be issued to the original payment method or bank account within 5–10 business days.
templates.privacy:
Privacy Policy for {shop}:

We are committed to safeguarding your privacy and personal data:

1. Information We Collect:
We collect information required to fulfill your orders, including your name, shipping address, phone number, and email address.

2. How We Use Your Information:
- To process, fulfill, and deliver your orders.
- To communicate updates regarding your shipment or support inquiries.
- To improve our storefront and services.

3. Data Security & Sharing:
We never sell or rent your personal information to third parties. Data is only shared with trusted delivery and payment partners to fulfill your purchase.
templates.terms:
Terms of Service for {shop}:

Welcome to our store. By accessing and purchasing from our store, you agree to the following terms:

1. Pricing & Payment:
All prices listed are accurate to the best of our knowledge. We reserve the right to correct pricing errors and cancel orders placed under erroneous terms.

2. Availability & Fulfillment:
All orders are subject to stock availability. In the event an item becomes unavailable, we will notify you promptly and offer a replacement or full refund.

3. Intellectual Property:
All content, photos, and branding on this store belong to the store owner and may not be reproduced without written permission.
templates.shipping:
Shipping & Delivery Policy for {shop}:

1. Processing & Delivery Times:
- Orders are processed and prepared within 24–48 business hours.
- Standard shipping takes 1–3 business days for major cities and 3–5 business days for other regions.

2. Shipping Rates:
Shipping charges are calculated and displayed at checkout before order finalization.

3. Shipment Tracking:
Once your order ships, you will receive an update with tracking details to follow your package until delivery.

shipping.zonesTitle: Your own delivery — zones and rates
shipping.zonesDescription: What you charge to deliver orders yourself. A zone is a set of destinations and the rate to reach them; the most specific match wins. Shipping companies price their own options and nothing here changes them.
shipping.noZonesBody: Without a zone your shop falls back to the flat rate below. Add zones when you want to charge different destinations differently.
shipping.zoneHasNoRate: No rate on this zone — checkout refuses orders to its destinations until you add one.
shipping.unzonedActiveDesc: Charged on every destination, because this shop has no zones.
shipping.unzonedShadowedDesc: Not charged. As soon as a shop has one zone, rates without a zone stop being used.
shipping.quickStartBody: One rate with no zone applies everywhere. It is the quickest way to make checkout work; you can split it into zones later.
shipping.zoneDialogHint: Name it for yourself — customers never see it.
shipping.countriesHint: Only these destinations match this zone.
shipping.citiesEmpty: Leave empty to cover every city in Palestine.
shipping.citiesHint: Only selected cities match this zone.
shipping.catchAllHint: Leave empty and this zone catches every destination no other zone covers. Keep exactly one of these.
shipping.catchAllConflict: “{name}” is already the catch-all. Give this zone its countries, or make “{name}” specific first.
shipping.priorityHint: Only breaks a tie between two equally specific zones. Lower wins.
shipping.rateDialogHint: What this zone charges for delivery.
shipping.unzonedRateHint: A rate with no zone. It applies everywhere, and only while the shop has no zones.
shipping.rateNameHint: Shown to the customer at checkout.
shipping.perKiloHint: Weight is rounded up to the next whole kilogram.
shipping.freeOverHint: Orders at or over this subtotal ship free. Leave empty for none.
shipping.deleteZoneBody: “{name}” and its rates are removed. Any destination it covered stops being quotable unless another zone catches it.
shipping.deleteRateBody: “{name}” is removed. If it was your only flat rate, orders go through with no delivery charge until you add another.
shipping.deleteLastRateTitle: This is the zone’s only rate
shipping.deleteLastRateBody: “{name}” is the only rate on “{zone}”. Without it, checkout refuses every order to that zone’s destinations. Add another rate first, or delete the zone itself.

diagnostics.nothingConfigured: No shipping is configured, so checkout cannot quote delivery to any address. Add a flat rate to start accepting orders.
diagnostics.noCatchAll: No catch-all zone. Any destination outside the countries you listed cannot be quoted. Add a zone with no countries selected.
diagnostics.multipleCatchAlls: More than one catch-all zone: {zones}. They match the same destinations, so only the one with the lowest priority is ever charged — give the others their countries or delete them.
diagnostics.unzonedShadowed: {count, plural, one {One rate has no zone and is no longer charged} other {# rates have no zone and are no longer charged}} — zones take over completely once one exists.
diagnostics.multipleRatesOnZone: Only the newest rate on a zone is charged. Extra rates on: {zones}
diagnostics.zoneWithoutRate: These zones match orders but carry no rate, so checkout refuses every order to their destinations: {zones}

mode.providerBody: Shipments are booked with a shipping company, which returns the tracking number and the label.

mode.notReady: This shop is set to ship through a carrier, but no carrier account is enabled and verified — shipments cannot be booked until one is.
mode.pricingNote: What the customer pays for shipping is always set by your own zones and rates below. A carrier changes who delivers, not the price.

carrier.noCarriersHint: You can keep delivering your own orders in the meantime — nothing else on this screen is affected.

carrier.verifyFirst: Verify these credentials before enabling the account — an unverified carrier fails at the first real shipment.

carrier.connectBody: Shipping is booked with the carrier under your own account, so the rates and the invoices are yours. Connect it here, then verify it.
carrier.connectFirst: Connect and verify a carrier account above to choose carriers and register your warehouses.
carrier.deleteConfirm: Remove this carrier account? Orders already booked keep their tracking, but nothing new can be booked until you connect one again.
carrier.onboardingTitle: How to connect your OTO account
carrier.onboardingDesc: OTO aggregates multiple carriers (Aramex, SMSA, SPL, DHL, etc.) under your own contract and negotiated rates.
carrier.onboardingStep1: Register or sign in to your account at OTO (tryoto.com).
carrier.onboardingStep2: From the OTO dashboard, go to Settings → Developers → Connected Apps / API Tokens.
carrier.onboardingStep3: Generate or copy your Refresh Token and paste it below.
carrier.onboardingStep4: Turn on Test mode (Sandbox) if you are testing, or turn it off for live shipments.

channels.merchantHint: Priced by your zones and rates below.
channels.carrierHint: Live prices from the carriers, charged to the customer exactly as quoted — you add nothing and lose nothing.

dnsIssues.DNS_PROXY_INTERCEPTING_SAME_PROVIDER: This domain resolves to {provider}’s network ({addresses}) rather than to your store, so no traffic reaches us and no certificate can be issued. {provider} also runs your DNS, so this is the proxy setting rather than the record: set it to DNS only. The record itself is correct and does not need changing.
dnsIssues.DNS_PROXY_INTERCEPTING_OTHER_PROVIDER: This domain resolves to {provider}’s network ({addresses}) rather than to your store, so no traffic reaches us and no certificate can be issued. Your DNS is not run by {provider}, so this is most likely a record still pointing at a previous host that sits behind {provider}. Check what your {required_type} record for “{required_name}” points at, and change it to {required_value}.
dnsIssues.DNS_DNSSEC_BOGUS: DNSSEC is switched on for this domain but is failing validation, so around two in five visitors cannot reach it at all — their internet provider refuses to look it up. This usually happens when nameservers or DNS records change while DNSSEC is still on. Turn DNSSEC off at the company you bought the domain from (the registrar, not your DNS host), then allow up to 24 hours for the old signature to expire.
dnsIssues.DNS_CAA_BLOCKED: A CAA record on “{owner}” says which certificate authorities may issue for this domain, and ours is not among them ({permitted}). No certificate can be issued until that record allows it. After you fix it, issuance can take up to an hour to retry.
dnsIssues.DNS_APEX_CNAME: The root of this domain has a CNAME record pointing at {value}. A root domain cannot use a CNAME, and it may stop other records in the zone from working.
dnsIssues.DNS_PROXY_POSSIBLE: If this record is proxied by {provider}, traffic will not reach your store. Set it to DNS only.
dnsIssues.DNS_WILDCARD_POINTS_AT_PLATFORM: Every name under this domain resolves here, including {probe_hostname}, which does not exist. That is a wildcard record (a record named “*”) pointing at your store, so a mistyped address and a subdomain you use for something else both land on it. Remove the wildcard and name the records you actually want.
dnsIssues.DNS_WILDCARD_CATCH_ALL: {probe_hostname} does not exist and still resolves, to {values}. Something between this domain and its visitors answers for every name — a wildcard record, or an internet provider that redirects unknown addresses. It is not pointing at your store, so it is not why the checks above read as they do.
